paragraphs.text: Use OpenCode Zen free models in DeepSeek Harness with anonymous access or an optional API key
# dsh-opencode-free
**English** | 繁體中文

Use free OpenCode Zen models in DeepSeek
Harness (DSH), without installing OpenCode or running a sep

arate server.
Anonymous access is the default; a Zen API key is optional.

- **Works on the anonymous tier.** Zen's free tier decides by request content
(tool declarations, an

`<env>` block, the TLS cipher list), not only by headers.
The plugin shapes anonymous requests to m

atch; see
what the free tier checks, with dated measurements.
- **No built-in model list.** The pick

er follows Zen's official model list: chat
models whose declared prices are all zero. Refreshes are

lazy, and a failed
refresh keeps the last good list. Hide individual models from the detail page.
-

**Native in DSH.** Models appear under **OpenCode Zen Free** with streaming,
reasoning, tool calls,

usage, and cancellation.
- **Availability checks.** The detail page shows probe results and latency.

Quota
limits and gate refusals do not remove models.
- **One release, one DSH.** Each release suppo
rts exactly one DSH version.

> [!WARNING]
> This is an unofficial plugin, not affiliated with OpenCode or DeepSeek.
> Anonymous a

ccess sends OpenCode CLI-format identity fields from this plugin,
> not the official CLI, and has no

third-party access guarantee: upstream changes
> may break it without notice. Anonymous
> quota is

shared by callers behind the same egress IP.
>
> The plugin runs with DSH's privileges and wraps pro

cess-wide HTTP entry points
> for the Zen inference endpoint. Read Security and limitations
> and DS

H's safety notice
> before installing.
## Quick start
### Requirements
| Requirement | Version |

| DeepSeek Harness | `0.2.2-alpha.2` (exact) |
| Node.js | `^22.19.0` or `>=24.0.0` |

Each release supports exactly one DSH version. Do not ignore peer dependency
warnings; all four runt

ime peers are required. For an older release, read its
GitHub Release or run
`npm view dsh-opencode-
free@<version> peerDependencies`.

## Usage

See the usage guide for refresh intervals, probe results,
cache recovery, and key verification.

The model picker shows the current catalogue rather than a fixed model list.
Context sizes, image su

pport, and reasoning levels come from each model's
published metadata. Failed refreshes preserve the

cached list; without a cache,
the plugin falls back to pi-ai's bundled models.

On the plugin detail page, enable or hide models and use **Probe now** to check
availability. Readin

g the model list also triggers a check once per local day.
**Checks send real inference requests and

consume quota**, one enabled model at
a time. Results persist across restarts.

Only catalogue withdrawal or explicit model unavailability removes a model;
gate refusals, exhausted

quota, invalid keys, and network failures are
inconclusive. See the catalogue decision rules
for re
fresh, removal, and cache behavior.
## Optional API key

Key priority: plugin `config.apiKey` → `OPENCODE_API_KEY` environment variable →
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

The implementation is based on the maintainer's analysis of the OpenCode CLI
source code and request

verification. It registers the
`opencode-zen-free` provider through DSH's `PiAiAdapter` and uses pi

-ai transports
to call `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1` directly. Tool execution stays in DSH.

Anonymous requests carry OpenCode CLI identity headers, a time-encoded session
ID, streaming, and su

bstantive `read` and `bash` tool declarations. The minimum
upstream admission rules are not fully ve

rified and may change. See the
protocol notes for sources and evidence limits.
### What changes in model requests

These adaptations apply only to anonymous requests; keyed requests retain their
original tools and p

daptations apply only to anonymous requests; keyed requests retain their
original tools and prompts.
| Adaptation | Model-visible effect |
| Windows shell | DSH's `pwsh` is presented as `bash`; returned calls are restored to `pwsh`. Read/s

hell parameter names are mapped while preserving host constraints. |
| Missing tools | Admission-onl
y `read`/`bash` declarations are added when absent. They grant no execution capability; calls to mis

sing tools are rejected before host dispatch. Explicit caller tool choices are preserved. |
| Compac
tion | Matching tool-less context-summary requests receive an OpenCode-style summary system prompt.
The user turn containing the conversation is unchanged. |

Tool guidance and admission declarations add tokens; compaction replaces system
prompt tokens. Tool/

history rewriting is prefix-stable for the same tool set,
but switching between anonymous and keyed

access changes that prefix.
Compaction is a separate request.
## Security and limitations

- **Process-wide interception:** the plugin wraps `globalThis.fetch` and
`node:http(s)` `request`/`g

et`, restricted to the HTTPS Zen inference origin
and `/inference/v1` path or descendants. Other plu

gins calling that endpoint
in the same process also receive the identity headers.
- **Profile depend

ency:** a `webServer` service is required for detail-page
routes. The built-in `headless` profile do

es not provide it.
- **Debug privacy:** `DSH_OPENCODE_FREE_DEBUG=1` enables diagnostics. Logs name
t

he credential kind (`anonymous` or `key`) and never any part of it. Upstream
refusals contribute onl

y the status, gate marker and error code, not their
text. Request and session identifiers still appe

ar, so do not publish raw logs.
- **Verification scope:** compat run results are not stored in the r

epository:
they depend on environment, versions, time and the shared anonymous quota. Run
the compat

guide yourself for current evidence. The
headless run does not verify Web, Desktop, or compaction.
